explanation: Service costs have been folded into Dutch menu prices since the 1970s, so restaurants rarely add a separate service charge and tipping is not required. Most people leave around 5-10% of the bill, or simply round up, when they're happy with the service, while leaving nothing for average service is completely normal and not seen as rude.
local_tip: Round up the bill or leave 5-10% in cash directly with the server if the service was good; otherwise, don't feel obligated to tip.

also_check.note: Tipping isn't expected in Japan and can confuse or embarrass staff since good service is already assumed and included in the price.
Tipping 15-20% is standard practice in US restaurants, where service staff often rely on tips to supplement a lower base wage.
A service charge is legally included in French bills, but rounding up or leaving small change for good service is a common courtesy.
